skin.setting: a riverboat casino on the Mississippi, 1904
skin.title: The Last Hand on the Delta Queen
skin.place: Aboard the Delta Queen riverboat casino, steaming up the Mississippi River
skin.styleGuide: Moody early Edwardian realism with gaslight amber tones, polished mahogany, river mist, velvet drapery, and vintage tintype textures.

rooms.name: the Grand Salon
rooms.description: A spacious dining and reception hall fitted with crystal chandeliers and round banquet tables.

rooms.name: the Central Hall
rooms.description: A long, wood-paneled corridor connecting the saloon deck to the riverfront exits.

rooms.name: the Card Parlor
rooms.description: An intimate lounge draped in green baize, designed for high-stakes poker and faro games.

rooms.name: the Owner's Stateroom
rooms.description: A lavish private suite adorned with brass fittings, where the owner's body was discovered.

rooms.name: the Gambling Saloon
rooms.description: The bustling main casino floor featuring roulette wheels, dice cages, and brass cashier cages.

rooms.name: the Velvet Lounge
rooms.description: A secluded smoking parlor with tufted velvet divans and heavy brocade curtains.

rooms.name: the Galley Pantry
rooms.description: A narrow service room stacked with silver dishware, liquor crates, and fresh linen.

rooms.name: the Promenade Deck
rooms.description: The open-air deck encircling the stern, offering cool river breezes and mist-slicked railings.

people.name: Captain Thaddeus Vance
people.bio: A stern river navigator whose family lost their river line to Calhoun in a ruthless foreclosure. He maintains rigid discipline aboard the boat despite his deep contempt for its owner.
people.voice: Speaks with a gravelly, authoritative baritone and nautical precision.
people.motive: Calhoun had threatened to revoke Vance's master license over an alleged navigational error unless Vance signed over his remaining family land.
people.portrait: A broad-shouldered man in his late fifties with a weathered face, a bushy gray beard, steel-gray eyes, wearing a double-breasted navy captain coat with tarnished brass buttons.

people.name: Clara Delacroix
people.bio: A sharp-witted gambler known from St. Louis to New Orleans for her ice-cold composure. She traveled under an assumed name to exploit Calhoun's lucrative high-stakes tables.
people.voice: Soft-spoken, elegant, and laced with a cool Southern drawl.
people.motive: Calhoun caught her marking cards earlier that week and demanded half of all her future tournament earnings under threat of exposure and jail.
people.portrait: A slender woman in her early thirties with dark pompadour hair, sharp arched eyebrows, dark piercing eyes, dressed in an emerald green silk evening gown with black lace trim.

people.name: Montgomery Pike
people.bio: A flamboyant speculator who treats the riverboat as his personal playground. His fortunes have turned sour following a disastrous trade in Memphis cotton futures.
people.voice: Loud, jovial, and quick with self-important pronouncements.
people.motive: Calhoun held promissory notes covering Pike's ruinous debts and was preparing to seize Pike's plantation at dawn.
people.portrait: A stout, florid-faced man in his mid-forties with a walrus mustache, thinning brown hair slicked back, wearing a cream linen suit, silk cravat, and pearl stickpin.

people.name: Beatrice Fontenot
people.bio: The Delta Queen's premier singer whose melancholic ballads enchant the salon nightly. Behind her glamorous persona lies a long-standing grievance over Calhoun's predatory contracts.
people.motive: Calhoun held her under an unbreakable exclusive performance contract while pocketing nearly all of her appearance fees.
people.portrait: A graceful woman in her late twenties with wavy auburn hair swept into an intricate updo, hazel eyes, wearing an embroidered burgundy velvet dress with beaded tassels.

people.name: Silas Sterling
people.bio: The vessel's meticulous accountant who manages every ticket, bet, and shipment aboard. He knows every secret transaction Calhoun conducted on the Mississippi.
people.voice: Precise, dry, and clipped, measuring every phrase carefully.
people.motive: Calhoun had discovered a discrepancy in the purser's ledgers and intended to make Sterling the scapegoat for his own tax fraud scheme.
people.portrait: A gaunt, clean-shaven man in his forties with wire-rimmed spectacles, slick black hair parted down the middle, wearing a dark gray woolen waistcoat and stiff white collar.

people.name: Roscoe Hayes
people.bio: A veteran dealer whose deft hands have managed dice and roulette wheels along the river for twenty years. He is fiercely protective of the vessel's gaming staff.
people.voice: Raspy, laconic, and punctuated by slow, deliberate cadences.
people.motive: Calhoun fired Hayes's younger brother without wages after a rigged game and barred him from working on the river.
people.portrait: A lean, tall man in his fifties with sunken cheeks, slicked silvering hair, a thin mustache, dressed in a formal black tuxedo with a crisp pleated shirt.

people.name: Jasper Calhoun
people.bio: A ruthless financier and owner of the Delta Queen, infamous for his predatory loans and cutthroat business tactics. His lifeless body was discovered in his private stateroom.
people.portrait: A heavy-set man in his sixties with slicked white hair, a trimmed goatee, cold hooded eyes, wearing an opulent black frock coat with silk lapels and a gold-threaded vest.

silence: I have already told you all my duties allowed me to observe, Inspector.
A lady never volunteers more gossip than necessary at the tables, sir.
My memory is entirely clear, Inspector, and I have nothing to add.
I was focused entirely on my melodies and the river, detective.
The ledger contains all relevant facts under my authority, sir.
House rules keep my eyes on the wheel, Inspector; I have nothing else for you.
skin.briefing: As the Delta Queen steams northward through thick river fog, the body of its owner, Jasper Calhoun, has been discovered dead in the Owner's Stateroom. The local marshal boarded at the midnight coal stop, sealing the vessel until the killer is uncovered. Six individuals had both access to the private quarters and grave reasons to wish Calhoun dead. Examine the vessel's deck logs, passenger testimony, and architectural constraints to determine the exact movements of every suspect and unmask the murderer.
skin.scene: The dim, gas-lit gaming saloon of a 1904 Mississippi paddle steamer, showing mahogany game tables, ornate brass chandeliers, heavy velvet curtains, and mist curling through open promenade windows.
